text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.58% today as oil prices climbed to a 6-week high following escalating military tensions between the U.S. and Iran in the Middle East over the weekend. Global crude hit $96 per barrel, driven by reports of Iranian attacks on U.S. Navy ships and strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities — events that tighten supply concerns and lift the outlook for oil producers' profits.

The stock has gained 1.27% over the past two weeks as these geopolitical risks have accumulated. Energy companies typically benefit when oil prices rise because higher crude values translate directly to stronger margins and cash flow, especially for integrated producers like ConocoPhillips that both drill and refine.
